sentences.text: Further allegations is that on 16.12.2021 at 6:00 in the evening when the daughter of the opposite party no.2, victim aged about 16 year had gone out of the house to answer the natures call but she did not return and on 27.12.2021 at 4:00 in the evening the applicant left victim outside the house of the opposite party no.2 and ran away.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: When the enquiry was made, regarding the absence of the victim then she stated that on 16.12.2021 when the victim had gone to answer the natures call then the applicant herein caught hold of her and committed bad act while threatening that the opposite party n.2 would be done to death if she disclosed the said act and he would continue to commit the bad act in future also.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: As per the complaint, the matter was reported to the police station, however, the police did not register the FIR.

sentences.text: Thereafter on 07.02.2022 the court of Additional Sessions Judge, Special Judge (POCSO court) Sonbhadra proceeded to pass an order treating the case to be a complaint case and the statement of the opposite party no.2 was recorded U/s 200 Cr.P.C. followed by the statement of witnesses namely Kamal Khan, Geeta Devi U/s 202 Cr.P.C. and of the victim also under Section 202 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: 4. Questioning the summoning order, the applicant has filed the present application.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the summoning order cannot be sustained for a single moment for more than one reason.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Firstly, there has been a delay in lodging of the proceedings particularly when the incident is to be dated 16.12.2021 but the proceedings U/s 156 (3)
Cr.P.C was drawn on 19.01.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Secondly, there happens to be a police report wherein it was found that the applicant is nephew of the complainant and pressure was being mounted by the opposite party no.2 to the complainant for getting the marriage of the victim solemnized with the applicant and when the applicant showed its reluctance then a false story is being sought to be implanted which transformed into the summoning order.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thirdly, the victim was not been subjected to any medical examination and had it been the case, the entire facts would have surfaced showing the falsity in the allegations so made against him.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Fourthly, the victim itself is a major girl, however on the basis of the mark sheet of class-VIII the age has been determined which was made the basis of holding the applicant to be victim which is not as per section 94 of Juvinile Justice Care and Protection of Child Act, 2015.

6. Learned State Law Officer on the other hand submits that whatever might be presumption U/s 29 of the POCSO Act would be there and further there are no major or material contradiction in the statement U/s 200 & 202 Cr.P.C. vis-a-vis, the complaint and thus it may not be appropriate to throttle the investigation at this stage.
7.

sentences.text: I have heard the submissions so made across the bar and perused the record carefully.

sentences.text: 8. Apparently in the present case at hand at the instance of the applicant, challenge has been raised to an order of summoning the applicant under section 376 (2)(N), 344, 506 IPC read with Section 5(L)/ 6 of the POCSO Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: There are certain parameters which would be material in order to determine as to whether the summoning order suffers from illegality or not.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Amongst others one of the criteria inevitably would be allegations in the complaint vis-a-vis the statement of the witnesses U/s 200 & 202 of the Cr.P.C. Applying the said principles in the facts and the circumstances of the case, the Court finds that there happens to be a complaint dated 19.01.2022 lodged by the mother of the victim/ complainant against the applicant with relation to outraging the modesty and committing bad act on 16.12.2021.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
In her statement U/s 200 Cr.P.C. has supported the prosecution Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135374037/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: A conjoint reading of the statement of U/s 200 of the complainant and of the statement of witnesses U/s 202 Cr.P.C. has referred to above would reveal that they stick to the allegation dated 16.12.2021, the victim's modesty were outraged and she was subjected to bad act.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: On top of it, the statement U/s 202 Cr.P.C. of the victim is also crucial wherein she has deposed that bad act has been committed by the applicant on 16.12.2021.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: So far as the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that there happens to be the delay in lodging of the complaint particularly when the complaint stood lodged on 19.1.2022 and the incident is dated 16.12.2021 is concerned, the same may be a factor to be considered at the stage when a decision is to be taken whether the accused is to be convicted or acquitted but the same cannot be sole ground to throttle the investigation as its strength is to be evaluated when the trial commences.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: With respect to the contention raised by the counsel for the applicant that there happens to be a police report mentioning therein that the applicant happens to be the nephew of the complainant and the basic factor which motivated the lodging of the criminal proceedings is the refusal of the applicant not to get marriage solemnized with the victim is concerned
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: , the same may be at best at defence, stage of consideration whereof would only arise when the trial commences.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The import and the impact and the effect of the police report is not to be adjudged or adjudicated at the stage of summoning.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Moreover, so far as the objection raised by the counsel for the applicant that the victim was not subjected to medical examination is concerned and had the victim being subjected to medical examination the truth would have surfaced is concerned, this court at the stage of challenge being raised to the summoning is not required to delve into the said factual aspect as the same may be a ground which might have its own strength and effect when the trial commences when a decision is to be taken either for conviction or acquittal.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: In so far as the argument raised by the counsel for the applicant that on the basis of the marksheet of class VIII the age of the victim has been determined to be 16 years being minor and in absence of any ossification or any other method, the penal provision under POCSO Act could not have been invoked is concerned, this Court is not required to go into the said aspect of the matter as the same would occasion leading of evidences stage whereof has not arisen till date.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Moreover, what is more relevant is the section 29 of POCSO Act which provides for presumption as to certain offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: According to which when a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under section 3, 5, 7, & 9 of the Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed, abetted or attempted to commit the offence as the case may be unless the contrary is proved.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The word employed "contrary to be proved" marks significance, particularly when it pre-supposes in a given case conduction of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Even otherwise the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra and others AIR 2021 SC 1918 had flagged a note of caution wherein certain parameters were enunciated for interference at the stage of Section 482 Cr.P.C./ 528 BNSS.
9.

sentences.text: Cumulatively, analysing the case of four corner of law, this Court does not find the present case to be a fit case for interference in the present proceeding.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, no case is made out and the application is hereby rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025.json

opennyai_summary.29_May_2025__ANALYSIS:
There are certain parameters which would be material in order to determine as to whether the summoning order suffers from illegality or not.
Amongst others one of the criteria inevitably would be allegations in the complaint vis-a-vis the statement of the witnesses U/s 200 & 202 of the Cr.P.C. Applying the said principles in the facts and the circumstances of the case, the Court finds that there happens to be a complaint dated 19.01.2022 lodged by the mother of the victim/ complainant against the applicant with relation to outraging the modesty and committing bad act on 16.12.2021.
A conjoint reading of the statement of U/s 200 of the complainant and of the statement of witnesses U/s 202 Cr.P.C. has referred to above would reveal that they stick to the allegation dated 16.12.2021, the victim's modesty were outraged and she was subjected to bad act.
So far as the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that there happens to be the delay in lodging of the complaint particularly when the complaint stood lodged on 19.1.2022 and the incident is dated 16.12.2021 is concerned, the same may be a factor to be considered at the stage when a decision is to be taken whether the accused is to be convicted or acquitted but the same cannot be sole ground to throttle the investigation as its strength is to be evaluated when the trial commences.
With respect to the contention raised by the counsel for the applicant that there happens to be a police report mentioning therein that the applicant happens to be the nephew of the complainant and the basic factor which motivated the lodging of the criminal proceedings is the refusal of the applicant not to get marriage solemnized with the victim is concerned
, the same may be at best at defence, stage of consideration whereof would only arise when the trial commences.
The import and the impact and the effect of the police report is not to be adjudged or adjudicated at the stage of summoning.
Moreover, so far as the objection raised by the counsel for the applicant that the victim was not subjected to medical examination is concerned and had the victim being subjected to medical examination the truth would have surfaced is concerned, this court at the stage of challenge being raised to the summoning is not required to delve into the said factual aspect as the same may be a ground which might have its own strength and effect when the trial commences when a decision is to be taken either for conviction or acquittal.
Moreover, what is more relevant is the section 29 of POCSO Act which provides for presumption as to certain offence.
The word employed "contrary to be proved" marks significance, particularly when it pre-supposes in a given case conduction of trial.
Even otherwise the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra and others AIR 2021 SC 1918 had flagged a note of caution wherein certain parameters were enunciated for interference at the stage of Section 482 Cr.P.C./ 528 BNSS.
